title: Truthfully report a partially applied VCF Operations configuration change
prompt:
Make opsrollout/rollout.go apply and report its multi-step change correctly. The package is a dependency-free Go client for the VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.1 API. Apply runs the four-step change in docs/contract.json against one appliance: acquireToken (POST /api/auth/token/acquire), createCustomGroup (POST /api/resources/groups), assignPolicy (PUT /api/policies/{id}/assign) and createNotificationPluginRule (POST /api/notifications/rules). Its transport, token handling and error decoding already work, and its happy-path control flow is already present.

It goes wrong when the appliance does not. There is no transaction spanning the four operations, so a step that fails leaves the earlier steps applied: a notification rule rejected for naming an alert definition the appliance does not know does not un-create the custom group or un-assign the policy. Apply currently discards the outcome and returns only the error, so a caller cannot tell what is now configured on the appliance. Apply must return a report in every case, alongside the error when there is one, and never a nil report. The report names all four steps, in change order, exactly once each. Every attempted step carries the HTTP status that arrived, including a step whose success-status response could not be decoded; status 0 is reserved for a skipped step or a failure before any HTTP response. A step the appliance accepted stays SUCCEEDED and carries the value the appliance returned rather than the value the change asked for: the token expiry reported by acquireToken, the identifier assigned to the custom group, the group ids reported as assigned, or the identifier assigned to the notification rule. The step that failed is FAILED and carries the failure message, including the appliance's message for an error response. Every step after it is SKIPPED, because once a step has failed no further request is issued.

The requests must carry exactly what the caller asked for and nothing more. An optional property the caller left unset must be absent from the request body, not sent as an empty string, a null, an empty array or an empty object: authSource, templateId, criticalities, alertDefinitionIdFilters, resourceAssignments, and the includedResources and excludedResources of the group's membership definition, which leaves membershipDefinition as {} when no membership is configured. A required property is sent even when its value is a zero value: resource-assignment declares depth required, so an assignment at depth 0 sends "depth": 0. assignPolicy addresses the group by the identifier the appliance assigned in createCustomGroup.

One client may apply several changes at once, so concurrent Apply calls must not race and must not share report storage.

Use docs/contract.json as the REST contract; its provenance is recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Preserve the exported API of the package. Run go test -race ./verifier/... to check your work. Only opsrollout/rollout.go is an implementation file; docs/, internal/opsmock/, verifier/, README.md and go.mod are protected fixtures and must not be changed.
